mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has stabilized near -21 percent after improving from -23.9 percent, showing a durable return of office commuting routines. This commuting base raises weekday footfall in retail-and-recreation districts, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains within [-23,-20] but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the commuting-recovery mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below -30 percent, travel capacity or willingness breaks down and cuts discretionary trips to retail venues. This produces lower RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT next weeks is below -30 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High RESIDENTIAL above 8 percent combined with GROCERY_PHARM recovering above -4 percent signals that household errand routines are normalizing while home-confinement persists. This combination lifts local retail-and-recreation trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL > 8 and GROCERY_PHARM > -4 both hold but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a no-new-restrictions reopening regime, TRANSIT above -26 percent and WORKPLACES above -22 percent jointly enable a broader return to out-of-home activity. This joint recovery drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the no-new-restrictions regime holds and TRANSIT > -26 with WORKPLACES > -22, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week PARKS drop greater than 10 percentage points signals a sharp withdrawal from outdoor discretionary activity. This withdrawal spills over to retail-and-recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:t-2w PARKS = 2.3 to t-1w PARKS = -13.9 is a 16.2-point drop
failure_condition: If PARKS drops more than 10 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The post-Easter school-holiday period in Sydney reduces discretionary retail-and-recreation trips as families return to routines and autumn weather cools. This seasonal downshift makes RETAIL_REC over the next week lower than the prior week.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-04-15 falls after Easter school holidays
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite the post-Easter school-holiday period, the seasonal mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Continued transit suppression below -25 percent reflects ongoing distancing policies and caution that keep retail-and-recreation capacity underused. RETAIL_REC therefore stays below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT < -25 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, the policy-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL staying above 9 percent indicates persistent work-from-home behavior that removes commuter footfall from retail-and-recreation districts. This behavior keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL > 9 and WORKPLACES remains below -20 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, the work-from-home mechanism is rejected.
